case_title: M/s Karnataka Emta Coal Mines Limited and Another v. Central Bureau of Investigation
statutory_provisions: Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988 – ss.13(1)(d)/13(2); Penal Code, 1860 – s.120-B r/w. ss.409/420; Mines and Minerals (Development & Regulation) Act, 1957
neutral_facts: The case involves a dispute between M/s Karnataka Emta Coal Mines Limited (KECML) and Karnataka Power Corporation Limited (KPCL) regarding the handling of coal rejects. The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) initiated proceedings against KECML based on an Audit Report by the Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG). The CBI alleged that KECML failed to account for coal rejects and that this constituted a breach of contract. The High Court had previously ruled that the CAG report could not form the basis for criminal proceedings. The Supreme Court examined whether the CBI's investigation was justified, considering the CAG report and the contractual agreements between the parties. The court found that the CBI's actions were based on an incorrect interpretation of the agreements and that the CAG report had not attained finality. The court concluded that the CBI's investigation was unfounded and quashed the charges framed against KECML.
